keyAndScale.primaryKey: C minor throughout, with power chords creating a modal ambiguity between natural minor and blues-inflected minor

scalesUsed.notes: C - D - Eb - F - G - Ab - Bb - C
scalesUsed.application: Primary scale for the song; the minor key combined with the relentless rhythm creates the intense, determined character perfectly suited to the Rocky III theme
The iconic single-note intro riff and guitar solo both draw from the minor pentatonic, giving the riffs their raw, aggressive simplicity

scalesUsed.notes: C - Eb - F - F#/Gb - G - Bb
scalesUsed.application: The added blue note (F#/Gb) appears in the guitar solo and some melodic fills, adding gritty tension to the minor pentatonic framework

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Aeolian (Natural Minor) with a raw, aggressive quality driven by the palm-muted single-note riff and power chord rhythm
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C minor is the relative minor of Eb major

mainProgression.description: The descending minor key progression that drives the verse and chorus, with the stepwise downward motion creating the relentless, determined momentum that defines the song.

sectionProgressions.description: The legendary single-note palm-muted riff on the low C string, one of the most instantly recognizable guitar intros in rock history
Palm-muted power chords with the descending C-Bb-Ab motion creating forward momentum, resolving back up to Bb for the turnaround
Ascending power chord build from Ab through Bb to Cm, creating the rising tension that launches into the explosive chorus

sectionProgressions.progression: Cm - Bb - Ab - Gm - Ab - Bb
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: i - VII - VI - v - VI - VII
sectionProgressions.description: Full power chord chorus with the classic descending-then-ascending motion and the anthemic 'It's the eye of the tiger' vocal hook
Return of the iconic single-note intro riff between verse-chorus cycles, resetting the energy before building again
Frankie Sullivan's lead guitar over the verse progression, using C minor pentatonic with aggressive bends and rhythmic phrasing

harmonicFunction: Cm (i) - Tonic minor chord, the dark, powerful foundation representing determination and intensity
Bb (VII) - Subtonic major, providing upward momentum and a sense of strength within the minor key
Ab (VI) - Submediant major, offering brightness and hope within the otherwise dark minor progression
Gm (v) - Dominant minor (instead of major V), maintaining the minor key character and avoiding too much brightness

techniques.name: Palm-Muted Single Note Riff
techniques.description: The legendary intro riff built on palm-muted single notes on the low strings, using rhythmic precision and muting control to create one of the most recognizable guitar hooks in rock history

notes: The riff is played entirely on the low A and D strings around the 3rd fret area
Primary notes: C (3rd fret A string), Eb (1st fret D string), F (3rd fret D string)
All notes are heavily palm muted for the tight, percussive 'chunka-chunka' sound
The rhythm uses syncopated eighth notes with rests creating the signature pattern
The riff resolves with an accented unmuted power chord hit on the downbeat
sequence: Place your palm firmly on the strings near the bridge for heavy muting
Pick the C note on the A string (3rd fret) with a sharp downstroke
Follow the rhythmic pattern: C-C-Eb-C-F-Eb-C with specific rhythmic spacing
Keep all notes short and percussive from the palm muting
End the riff phrase with an unmuted C5 power chord accent for the dynamic punch
tips: The palm muting is the most important element - without it, the riff loses its character
Keep the muting pressure consistent so all notes have the same short, percussive quality
Use all downstrokes for the heaviest, most aggressive attack
Practice the rhythmic pattern slowly with a metronome until it is completely locked in
This riff is beginner-friendly in terms of fretting but requires good right-hand muting control

techniques.name: Power Chord Verse and Chorus
techniques.description: Driving power chord rhythm using Cm, Bb, Ab, and Gm shapes that provide the harmonic backdrop for verse and chorus, played with a mix of palm muting and open strumming

notes: C5: X-3-5-5-X-X (A-string root) or 8-10-10-X-X-X (E-string root)
Bb5: 6-8-8-X-X-X (E-string root) or X-1-3-3-X-X (A-string root)
Ab5: 4-6-6-X-X-X (E-string root)
G5: 3-5-5-X-X-X (E-string root)
The verse uses palm-muted power chords while the chorus opens up to full strumming
sequence: Play the verse with palm-muted downstroke power chords on C5-Bb5-Ab5
Use the descending power chord motion to create forward momentum
Release palm muting for accent hits on the last beat of phrases
Open up completely for the chorus with full, ringing power chord strumming
Return to the palm-muted single-note riff for interludes
tips: The E-string root power chord shapes allow easy sliding between Cm, Bb, Ab, and Gm
Keep the verse power chords tight and percussive with palm muting
The chorus should feel like a release of all the tension built in the verse
Practice the three-fret and two-fret power chord slides for smooth transitions
details.progression: C5 - Bb5 - Ab5 - G5 (descending power chord sequence)

techniques.name: Rhythmic Accents and Dynamic Control
techniques.description: The precise rhythmic accent patterns that give the song its driving, determined feel - alternating between muted and accented notes to create the signature pumping rhythm

notes: The song alternates between palm-muted passages and sharp accent hits
Accents typically fall on beats 1 and 3 for a strong, march-like feel
The pre-chorus uses ascending accented chords for the energy build
Dynamics shift dramatically between the muted verse riff and the open chorus
The interlude riff returns to palm-muted single notes resetting the dynamic level
sequence: During the verse, accent the first beat of each power chord change
Keep the in-between beats tightly palm muted for contrast
In the pre-chorus, increase both volume and accent intensity progressively
Hit the chorus with full, unrestrained power chord strumming
Return to the dynamic starting point for each verse-chorus cycle
tips: Think of the dynamics as a boxer's training montage - start restrained, build to peak energy
The contrast between muted and accented hits is what creates the song's iconic pump
Use your picking hand to control dynamics rather than relying solely on pedal or amp settings
The song should feel relentless but controlled - never sloppy or out of control
details.progression: Accented C5 - Bb5 - Ab5 with palm-muted fills

sections.name: Intro Riff
sections.description: The legendary palm-muted single-note riff that opens the song. Instantly recognizable from the Rocky III soundtrack, this riff is one of the most iconic guitar hooks in rock history.
notes: Heavy palm muting creates the tight, percussive character
All notes played on the A and D strings in the 1st-3rd fret area
The syncopated rhythm with rests is as important as the notes themselves
The riff builds with the band entering gradually over the repeated pattern

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Palm-muted power chords drive the verse with the descending C-Bb-Ab progression, creating the determined, forward-moving feel beneath the vocal story.
notes: Palm-muted power chords maintain the tight, controlled verse energy
The descending chord motion mirrors the fighter's determination
Keep dynamics restrained compared to the chorus for proper contrast
The turnaround back to Bb sets up the return to Cm

sections.name: Pre-Chorus
sections.description: The ascending power chord build from Ab through Bb to Cm, increasing in intensity and volume to launch into the massive chorus.
notes: Release palm muting progressively as the section builds
The ascending Ab-Bb-Cm motion creates natural rising energy
Increase strumming intensity and volume with each chord change
The final Cm hit should ring full and unmuted to launch the chorus

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The explosive arena rock chorus with full power chord strumming and the iconic 'It's the eye of the tiger' vocal hook at maximum energy.
sections.progression: Cm - Bb - Ab - Gm - Ab - Bb
notes: Full, unmuted power chord strumming at maximum intensity
The descending Cm-Bb-Ab-Gm creates the dramatic chorus sweep
The ascending Ab-Bb turnaround propels back into the next section
This is the crowd singalong moment - play with full arena-filling energy

sections.name: Interlude
sections.description: Return of the iconic single-note intro riff between verse-chorus cycles, resetting the dynamic energy level before the next build.
notes: Return to the palm-muted single-note riff from the intro
The dynamic drop from the chorus to the riff creates effective contrast
Maintain the tight, percussive palm muting quality
This interlude resets the energy for the next verse-chorus cycle

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Frankie Sullivan's guitar solo over the verse progression, using C minor pentatonic with aggressive bends, rhythmic phrasing, and blues-inflected lead lines.
sections.progression: Cm - Bb - Ab - Bb (solo over verse changes)
notes: Solo uses C minor pentatonic primarily at the 8th and 11th positions
Aggressive bends and fast vibrato define the intense phrasing
The lead lines mirror the determined, aggressive character of the song
Rhythm guitar maintains palm-muted power chord support underneath

sections.name: Final Chorus
sections.description: The final chorus repetitions at peak intensity, building to the climactic ending with repeated vocal hooks and full-power instrumentation.
sections.progression: Cm - Bb - Ab - Gm - Ab - Bb
notes: Maximum energy maintained through multiple chorus repetitions
The vocal hooks repeat with increasing intensity and crowd participation
Full power chord strumming with no restraint through the final section
The song ends with a final emphatic Cm power chord hit and cymbal crash

guitar.recommended: Gibson Les Paul or Gibson SG for the warm, thick humbucker tone
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for the tight palm-muted riff and power chord rhythm; the thick humbucker tone is essential for the heavy muted sound

amp.recommended: Marshall JCM800 for the tight, punchy early-80s rock tone

settings.gain: 5-6 (moderate gain for defined palm muting without excessive saturation)
settings.treble: 6 (bright enough for note definition in muted passages)
settings.middle: 7 (strong midrange for the punchy, aggressive tone)
settings.bass: 5 (solid but tight - too much bass will blur the palm-muted riff)
settings.presence: 6 (clear and present for the picking attack to cut through)

effects.distortion: Moderate gain from the amp. The riff needs enough crunch for power but enough clarity for the palm-muted single notes to be defined.
effects.delay: Minimal or no delay for the rhythm parts. Short delay (200ms) can enhance the solo tone.
effects.reverb: Short to medium room reverb for natural ambiance without washing out the tight muted rhythm
effects.other: A noise gate can help keep the palm-muted riff clean by eliminating string noise between notes. A compressor can even out the dynamics between muted and accented passages.

beginner.focus: Learn the iconic single-note intro riff and basic power chord shapes
steps: Master the palm-muted single-note intro riff at slow tempo
Learn C5, Bb5, Ab5, and G5 power chord shapes on the E string
Practice transitioning between the single-note riff and power chords
Play the verse progression (Cm-Bb-Ab-Bb) with simple palm-muted strumming
beginner.timeEstimate: 1-2 weeks for intro riff and basic progression

intermediate.focus: Add the full song structure with dynamic accents and complete verse-chorus pattern
steps: Refine the palm muting control for consistent verse rhythm
Learn the pre-chorus ascending build with increasing dynamics
Practice the full chorus power chord progression with open strumming
Play through the complete song structure with proper dynamic contrast
intermediate.timeEstimate: 2-3 weeks for full song with dynamics

advanced.focus: Master the guitar solo, rhythmic precision, and performance-level energy
steps: Learn the guitar solo using C minor pentatonic and blues scale at the 8th position
Practice aggressive bending and vibrato techniques for the solo style
Refine the rhythmic accent patterns for maximum groove and impact
Perform the complete song with seamless transitions and stage-level energy

commonMistakes: Insufficient palm muting on the intro riff - the muting is what makes the riff iconic, not just the notes
Using too much gain which blurs the palm-muted riff into an indistinct chug
Not enough dynamic contrast between the muted verse and open chorus sections
Playing the riff with upstrokes or alternate picking instead of aggressive all-downstrokes
practiceRoutine: Warm up with the palm-muted single-note riff at 80 BPM, focusing on muting consistency (5 minutes)
Practice C5-Bb5-Ab5 power chord transitions on the E string at 90 BPM (5 minutes)
Work on the verse-to-chorus dynamic transition with tone and volume changes (5 minutes)
Practice the pre-chorus ascending build with proper accent placement (5 minutes)
Play through the complete song with a backing track at 109 BPM (5 minutes)
focusAreas: Tight, consistent palm muting for the intro riff and verse sections
Clean power chord transitions sliding along the E string
Dynamic contrast between the four main dynamic levels: riff, verse, pre-chorus, chorus
Rhythmic precision at 109 BPM with locked-in downstroke timing
metronomeWork: Start the palm-muted riff at 80 BPM, building to 109 BPM in 5-10 BPM increments
Practice power chord verse rhythm at 109 BPM with accent on beat 1
Work on the full dynamic cycle (riff-verse-prechorus-chorus) at 100 BPM before full tempo
Full song run-through at 109 BPM once all sections are locked in
